lines: Friday, 15 May 2026
Housekeeping
PRESIDENT:  This is the second day of the
evidentiary hearing in DIAC case no. 240079
between China State Construction Engineering
Corporation (Middle East) LLC and Dubai
Integrated Economic Zones Authority.
Before we recall Mr Feng, are there any
points of housekeeping?  None, I believe, from
the tribunal.
MS CHENG:  There is a very small one in
relation to the parties' new contemporaneous
documents.  I think we've confirmed to those
instructing my learned friend that we have no
objection to his two documents, but we've yet
to hear about ours.
MR RIGNEY:  (Inaudible: off microphone).
MS CHENG:  And the second point, and I am
remiss for mentioning it second, is that
I ought to introduce to you my junior,
Dr Nicholas Maciolek, with whom I will appear
for the rest of the hearing.
PRESIDENT:  He's probably fed up of seeing
me, because he had the disadvantage of being in
front of me last week.  I'm not surprised
he couldn't face a Monday!
All right.  Thank you very much.  Well,
then, if there's nothing else, Mr Feng.
MR FENG RUI (continued)
WITNESS:  Good morning, sir.
PRESIDENT:  Good morning, Mr Feng.  I hope
you had a restful evening.
WITNESS:  Not really.  Jet lag, so I woke
up at 4.00.  I think the rest of the colleagues
from Dubai also have the same issue.
PRESIDENT:  Yes.  Well, I'm sorry to hear
that.  But I don't think you've got too much
more ahead of you by way of giving evidence
today.
Can I just remind you that the affirmation
you gave yesterday still applies.  Thank you.
Yes.  Mr Rigney.
Cross-examination by MR RIGNEY (continued)
MR RIGNEY:  Mr Feng, I was about to move
to the topic of traffic coating at the close of
yesterday, and what I wanted to ask you at
the outset is whether you have any personal
recollection of the timescale over which the
traffic coating was laid?
A    Not really.
Q    You have no personal knowledge?
A    The site works actually is handled by
the -- by my site team.
Q    Right.
A    I know this traffic coating was done at
a very later stage, as -- you know, as one of
the finishing works.
Q    So there's no point in me taking you
through the documents, because all we'd be doing is
looking at documents with which you're not familiar;
is that right?
A    For sure I have already reviewed
the documents.
Q    You've reviewed the documents, but you
have no personal knowledge of what it is that was
being done or when, have you?
A    There are some interfaces.  For example,
the client, one time they show me -- Engineer Yaser
and Engineer Abduljalil show me the glossy finish of
the driveway epoxy, and they are not happy with
that, and I have explained this is because of the
design of the basement is not flat.  We have to
design the basement with a certain grade so that it
allowed the wastewater and the rainwater to properly
drain to the drainage.
So even though I, as a goodwill,
I offered them to replace that with a matte finish
for the driveway area.  And eventually we have done
a piece of mockup and they have accepted that.
Q    Well, Mr Feng, that's a specific aspect
that I think you are referring to.
Could we please look at paragraph 496
of your first witness statement, and could we go,
please, to {C4-87}.
A    Paragraph?
Q    If you would look, please, at
paragraph 496.  You say:
"Even though this was a design
matter, and not our responsibility, I agreed in good
faith to re-coat a portion of the car park with
a matte finish."
A    Yes.
Q    "This work was done, inspected, and signed
off by the Engineer in early 2019."
A    Yes.
Q    That's the matter you've just been
referring to, I think, isn't it?
A    Yes.
Q    It wasn't carried out in early 2019,
was it?  It was a little bit later than that, wasn't
it?
A    Can you show me this exhibit FR-122?
Q    Well, first of all, can I just check your
recollection?  I'm suggesting to you that your
timescale of "early 2019" is incorrect, and that in
fact the work was being carried out as late as
September 2019.  Do you agree with that or not?
A    I do not agree with that.
Q    You don't.  Okay.
A    Maybe the inspection recorded as
September 2019.  I have not -- I'm not sure which
part you were referring to, September 2019, but
I believe the work is done quite so.  You know,
progress of this -- it's a big basement, it's not
done in one day.
Q    Of course.
Could we have a look at one of the
documents, please.  Could we look at {D1776.1}.  And
could we just look at this together, Mr Feng.
You can see this is an inspection
request, isn't it?  Yes?  Do you see that, Mr Feng?
A    Yes.
Q    And you see that it's dated
14 September 2019, don't you?  Do you see that?
The top right-hand corner?
A    Yes.
Q    14 September 2019, isn't it?
A    Sir, can I ask if this is referred to my
witness statement?
Q    No, no, I'm not talking about your witness
statement.
A    Can you scroll down?  Please can you
scroll down?
Q    I wonder if you would just answer
the questions for a moment.
A    Sir, I --
Q    I suggest we look at the document,
Mr Feng.
A    Sir, yesterday as I explained, I have
managed the site as a general manager, right?  So
I do not personally involve or record every single
submissions.  From these submissions, the IR
request, as I explained just now, I'm not really
aware of this submission because this is not signed
by me, or I do not recall this submission.
Q    Does it follow that you weren't personally
aware when you stated in your witness statement that
it was "signed off by the Engineer in early 2019"?
A    Can you refer to the --
Q    Paragraph 496 of your witness statement.
A    Yes.  Can you refer to that 200 --
my witness statement exhibit 122?
Q    If you look at paragraph 496, you say:
"This work was done, inspected, and
signed off by the Engineer in early 2019."
A    Yes.
Q    When you made that statement, was it
a statement from your own personal knowledge,
Mr Feng?
A    As I explained, this is a big -- it's
a big basement.  As far as I'm aware, the work
starts to paint in early 2019.  Can you -- if you
want to cross-check, can you open this exhibit 122?
Q    No.  What I'd like to do is to take you,
please, to the document, back to {D1776.1}, please.
A    As I --
Q    I think actually it's the document you
want to go to.  But if we just look at this, please.
A    Yes.  As I mentioned, this is not signed
by me.  This is by our technical --
Q    This is by the engineer, isn't it?  Let's
just look, please, at the document.  It's dated
14 September 2019.
PRESIDENT:  Sorry, Mr Rigney.  It might be
by the engineer, but I think what the witness
was saying is that the contractor's signature
on this is not his signature.  I think that was
the point he was just making.
MR RIGNEY:  Fine.
But so far as the -- if we could just
scroll down a little, please.  We've seen the
date of 14 September.  And then, please, if we
look at the nature of the request -- if we just
scroll back up a little bit, please.  Sorry.
Perfect.  Thank you very much.  We can see that
the request is:
"We hereby invite you for the Inspection
of Rectification of Polyurethane Coating
application for Driveway at ..."
Now, that's the coating that you're
referring to in your witness statement,
isn't it, at paragraph 496?
A    The National -- epoxy coating applied in
the basement in different -- in progress.
Q    Yes.
A    And so this particular -- if you look at
this particular inspection record, though it's not
signed by me, but it's qualified that it only refers
to D1-LG area.  There are many runs of -- for this
finishing work, there are many runs of, you know,
rectifications.  I assume this is one of the -- you
know, the repainting of this area.  Because, to be
honest, at that time this -- the building has
already been substantially completed.  For me, it's
a little bit strange to see an inspection record in
September 2019.
Q    We can see that this is a request from
China State which is dated 14 September 2019,
can't we?
A    Yes, I agree.
Q    So it looks as though at least that part
of the work which is described in the document was
being carried out at that date, doesn't it?
A    It's only for D1-LG.
Q    Yes.
A    We have 23 buildings, sir.
Q    Well, I can see that it's a process over
time, Mr Feng.  I wonder whether perhaps then
we might go to --
A    Can we refer to my exhibit 122?
Q    I think this is the document in question.
A    This is the document?
Q    Yes.  It's referred to in your witness
statement.
PRESIDENT:  Is that right?
MR RIGNEY:  I think it is.  Maybe
I'm wrong about that.
PRESIDENT:  Let me check.  (Pause)
MR RIGNEY:  Sir, it is.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.
MR RIGNEY:  I thought it was.
MR THOMAS:  Can I just be clear of whether
the driveway referred to here at D1-LG, whether
that's part of the car park at the basement
level of the podium?
A    Yes, so in simple terms, sir, we defined
the entire basement: some area is like a parking
lot, and adjacent to that is a common driveway for
cars to go along.  And there are certain area come
to the entrance when we have the sidewalk, which is
a slightly higher level, like 150mm higher: that is
for pedestrians to access to the building.
MR THOMAS:  Yes.
A    So the driveway that has been repainted is
for the car park driveway, not for the parking lot
itself.
MR THOMAS:  It's an entrance or exit to
the car park?
A    No, it's the entire driveway of
the basement.
MR THOMAS:  Of the basement car park?
A    Yes.
MR THOMAS:  Yes, okay.  Thank you.
MR RIGNEY:  Mr Feng, I wonder whether
you could just confirm: the reference to "LG"
in box number 1, that's a reference to "lower
ground", isn't it?
A    "D1-LG": that is the building D1 area,
lower ground.
Q    Lower ground.
Could we just scroll down, please, in
the document, to the next page, please, page 2.
That gives us, I think, doesn't it, the plan of
the area in question?
A    Yes.
Q    And if we could just look, please, in
the bottom right-hand corner.
A    Yes.
Q    It's right, isn't it, that the area in
question is in the "Lower Ground Floor Plan"?
A    Yes.
Q    And we can see what it is that is
the subject of the request.  Do you see the work
highlighted in yellow?
A    Yes.  This is one example of this work.
Q    That's where the work was being done in
relation to which the inspection request was raised,
isn't it?
A    Sir, there are two things.
First, the client raised some
concerns about this glossy finish.  So I had
a discussion with the client on site and offered
them, as a goodwill, to repaint the driveway with
a matte finish.  This is something I recall.
But for the exact timing, as far as
I recall, it's early September.  How this particular
inspection record is recorded in September -- in
early 2019.  How this is recorded in this particular
IR, only submitted in September 2019, to be frank,
I have not really --
Q    Well, this is the IR that's referred to at
footnote 235 at paragraph 495 of your witness
statement, isn't it, Mr Feng?
A    I believe there are many other errors
related to this epoxy, this -- I can assure you the
basement car park epoxy finished quite -- in early
2019; otherwise we cannot get even the DCD approval.
The DCD won't really approve this if they see a bare
concrete finish.
Q    Can we just look a little bit further just
to see what we are looking at.  I want to just come
back again to 496, please.  Could you please scroll
down to page 3 of the document.  I think if you
could just turn that 90 degrees to the left, please.
That's it, thank you.
A    Yes.
Q    So if we just scroll down through the
photographs.  I just want to make sure that you
agree that this is the area that was the subject of
the inspection request.  The photographs I think
correspond to the shaded areas in the drawing that
we just looked at, don't they?
A    Yes.
Q    That's fine.  Thank you very much.  So
that's the area, isn't it?
A    Yes.
Q    Shall we then scroll down a little bit
more to see the work that was being done?
A    Yes, and you can see from the photos
below -- can you just go back to the previous page.
Yes, this one.  From this page, you can see there's
a white-colour pattern, there's a green-colour
patter.  The green-colour pattern is the previous
epoxy we have done.
So the clients are not satisfied with
the finishes.  I offered, as goodwill, to re-do the
paint.  So that's the process when they, you know,
re-do the epoxy painting with some matte finish.
I remember the mockup.  I offered
them a mockup.  The mockup is not at this area.
That mockup happened in early 2019.
Q    Yes.  And then if we go back to the first
page of the document, please.
So, Mr Feng, we've looked at the area
on the drawings where the work was being carried
out, we've looked at the photographs of that area
and we've looked at the photographs of the work
actually being carried out, haven't we?  Agreed,
Mr Feng?
A    This says -- I didn't submit this one, so
I cannot really comment.
Q    We'll come back to that in a moment,
Mr Feng.  Can we just agree that we've looked at
the area on the floor plan where the work was being
carried out; yes or no?
A    Yes.
Q    We've looked at photographs of that area,
haven't we?
A    Yes.
Q    And we've looked at the work which was
being carried out, haven't we?
A    Yes.
Q    Now, if we scroll back to page 1, we can
see that that work was ready for inspection on
14 September, wasn't it?
A    This -- again, as I explained, when we
finished the work much earlier and we only offered
for inspection on that date, why this is submitted
so late, in September 2019, to be frank, I really
don't recall.
Q    Mr Feng, did you read this document when
you referred to it in footnote 235 of your witness
statement?
A    Yes, I read the document.
Q    Well, your witness statement says that
the work in question was:
"... inspected, and signed off by
the Engineer in early 2019."
And in support of that statement
you've exhibited a document which demonstrates that
the inspection request was dated 14 September 2019.
A    Sir, if you look at this document itself,
the -- it's submitted in August.
Q    The document is dated 14 September, is it
not?
A    Can we scroll up?
Q    Top right-hand corner:
Yes?
A    Yes.
Q    And if we just check, if we could go down,
please, to the "Comments" box, the comments are
dated 21 September 2019, aren't they?
Do you agree?
A    Yes, I agree.
Q    And when you look in the comments,
Mr Feng, you can see that the rectification works
are said to be ongoing, aren't they?
A    This is just an ongoing repaint of
the driveway.
Q    Yes.  But you see, you rely upon this
document in support of what you say at
paragraph 496.  Could we just go back to
paragraph 496, please.  You say:
"This ... was done, inspected, and
signed off by the Engineer in early 2019."
And I think, Mr Feng, we can see from
this document that that statement isn't correct,
is it?
A    I cannot remember exactly of this
particular document.
Q    It's right, isn't it, that work in fact
continued into October 2019, didn't it?
A    No, this is not correct.
Q    Well, do you have personal recollection to
the effect that the work finished before
October 2019, Mr Feng?
A    It is finished before October 2019,
otherwise how we get the authority approval?
Q    Can we go then, please, to {D1776.2}.
A    I still doubt this is the document.
Q    If you would be good enough, please, to
look at this document, Mr Feng.  It's another field
inspection request, and we can see that the date of
the document is 7 October 2019, isn't it?  Do you
see that?
A    Mm-hm.
Q    And then, please, if you would look at
the "Description of [the] Task", it says:
"We hereby invite you for the
Inspection of Rectification of Polyurethane Coating
application for Driveway ..."
So it's the same work, isn't it, but
it's the subject of a request in October 2019?
A    As I told you, the original finish is
a glossy finish.  I have goodwill offered them to
make it a matte finish.  So this work is just
a rework of the completion -- of the completed work.
Q    And it's right, Mr Feng -- I'm not going
to take you to the documents, I'm just going to give
the tribunal references -- there are further
documents indicating later requests in October:
{D1776.3}, {D1776.4}, dated 10 and 16 October.
But the consequence of that, Mr Feng,
is that the statement you made only a few seconds
ago that you were sure that work didn't continue
until October was incorrect, wasn't it?
A    This is just the rectification works; it's
not the initial works.
MS CHENG:  Sir, I think the witness has
answered this question.
MR RIGNEY:  Well, he has not answered that
question actually.
I wonder whether you would answer
the question, Mr Feng.
A    As I explained, this is just the
rectification works.  It's not even signed by me.
Q    But we agreed that the inspection report
in September was the inspection report that was
referred to in your footnote, and we agreed that
that was the work that you had in mind when you were
commenting upon it at paragraph 496, didn't we?
A    Maybe I have made a mistake in this
reference.  But what I can confirm is: the work has
started to apply the matte finish epoxy coating in
early September.
Q    The mistake that you've made, Mr Feng, is
in your witness statement at paragraph 496,
isn't it?
A    Yes.
Q    And the mistake is that you said that
the work completed "in early 2019", and it didn't.
It went on until October 2019, didn't it?
A    No, I do not agree.  As you can see, this
is just rectification works.  It's the repainting of
it.  It's not: I have not finished my work.  It's
the goodwill.  And now you blame me that
the goodwill is not complete.
Q    Very well.
Can we just turn on to an allied and
related topic, Mr Feng, just slightly different, and
that's going back more generally to the traffic
coating.
Do you know from your personal
knowledge the broad timescales during which
the coating was laid?  Going back to the question
I started with this morning.
A    The exact timing, I cannot remember
exactly.  But I can confirm that this has been
applied over a substantial duration, because the
basement is a common area, you know: there are many
things affecting the application -- continuous
application of the epoxy.  So we have to relocate
the storage from one area to the other, and to allow
them -- to allow the epoxy can be applied in
a relatively clean and, you know, settled,
satisfactory, favourable condition on site.
The coating is always -- like
the painting, is always the last piece of finishing
works.  And this -- what, sir, you have shared is,
as I have explained, this is the rectification works
to change the glossy finish to a matte finish.  For
the glossy finish, which perfectly complies with
the specification and serves the purpose of the
building, has already been done before in early
September.
Q    Very well.
Can we just think about the traffic
coating, Mr Feng.  It was put down, wasn't it, in
three layers; is that right?
A    Yes, as far as I track this, the record is
like that.
Q    There was a primer coat, wasn't there?
A    Mm-hm.
Q    Sorry, do you agree: there was a primer
coat?
A    Yes.
Q    Yes.  There was then a first coat, wasn't
there?
A    Yes.
Q    And then there was a second coat, wasn't
there?
A    Correct.
Q    Yes.  And the primer coat started to go
down in May 2018, didn't it?
A    I cannot remember exactly dates.
Q    Okay.  And the second coat, that was
completed -- or at least, I think, the last IR for
the second coat was round about August 2019,
wasn't it?
A    Sir, as I explained, this is a big
basement: we do the applications in different
stages, part by part.  So we cannot really rely on
one FIR to confirm the timing, the exact timing of
application works.
Q    Mr Feng, perhaps we should just go to what
I think is the last of the IRs for the second coat.
Could we go, please, to {D1774.28}.
A    Sir, can we refer to my witness statement?
Q    No, we're going to look at some documents,
Mr Feng.  And I hope you're going to be able to help
me; if you can't, you must say so.
PRESIDENT:  Sorry to interrupt.
Mr Feng, as I think I said yesterday, when
Mr Rigney has finished asking you questions,
then Ms Cheng will have the opportunity to ask
you questions to give us a more complete
picture.
WITNESS:  Sure.
PRESIDENT:  So for the moment, we'll let
Mr Rigney take his course.
MR RIGNEY:  Thank you.
Mr Feng, I'm not trying to be difficult,
but there's just some information I'd like from
you, and some evidence from you, for the
assistance of the tribunal.  That's why I'm
asking the questions.
What I'd just like your assistance on now,
please, is the document which we can see is
dated 1 August 2019.  Do you see that in
the top right-hand corner?
A    Yes.
Q    And then, please, if you would look at the
"Description of [the] Task" box, you can see that
it's an invitation:
"... for the Inspection of [the] 2nd
coat Final paint of [the] ... polyurethane ...
completion at Driveway and Ramp Area ..."
Do you see that?
A    Yes.
Q    So we're still talking about the basement,
aren't we?  You agree with that?
A    Yes.
Q    And this is the "2nd coat Final paint",
isn't it?
A    Can we scroll down to see the area?
Q    Of course.  Could we just scroll down,
please.  Those are the areas that are the subject of
the request, aren't they, the shaded --
A    Yes, so on the right, the three --
four marked areas actually, that is in hotel
building.  And this part is also in the D4, which is
the hotel part of the building.
Q    But nevertheless -- if we could just go
back, please, to page 1 -- the second coat is the
subject of an inspection request in the first box,
which means it was still --
A    Sir, this inspection report is for
milestone C, not milestone B.  As I explained, this
is the hotel basement.  The drawing attached is
already showing this as the hotel basement.
Q    Very well.  But on the basis that this
appears to be the last of the IRs so far as this
work is concerned --
A    Sir, we are talking about four milestones.
Q    Very soon afterwards, Mr Feng, there were
problems with it, after the application, weren't
there?
A    No, I do not agree this allegation.
Q    Could we go, then, please, to {D603}, and
can we look at this document together, Mr Feng.
We can see that it's from DAR and it's addressed to
you, isn't it?
A    Mm.
Q    Yes.  Do you remember this document,
Mr Feng?
A    Mm.
Q    Yes.  You can see the date of the letter
is 10 September 2019, isn't it?
A    Mm-hm.
Q    Shall we just look to see what it says?
First of all, the subject is "Rejected Works",
isn't it?
A    Mm.
Q    And if we look to see which works are
rejected, you can see that amongst the four items
that are set out in the bullet points, the first is
the "Basement flooring surfaces".  Do you see that?
A    Sir, during that time there are many
correspondence between us, the engineer and
the employer.  They have made some -- as far as
I recall, there are some, you know, very general
statements from the employer's side, not satisfied
with the workmanship, and which we have also
responded one by one.
So for me, this is a big site.  If we
just put a very general claim, it's not helpful.
We have to be proactive, it has to be accurate,
point out what are, you know, the problems that is
related with the work.
We have to be specific.  Exactly like
the FIR you just mentioned: it's right it's for
the basement, but it's not for milestone B or
milestone A; instead it's for milestone C, which is
the hotel building.  So if you do not look into the
detail of the submissions, you can easily be
misguided by the document itself.
I was on site on a daily basis:
I know what is happening.  As far as I recall,
I have done the epoxy painting for the entire
19 buildings, including the art(?) building, in
early September -- in early March 2019.
Q    Very well.
Mr Feng, can we just cover one last
topic, please.  I don't think I need to ask you
anything more about the basement.
Could we please just look at your
first statement, please, at paragraph 160, {C4-27}.
Q    {C4-27}, your first witness statement,
paragraph 160, Mr Feng.  It's a slightly different
topic: I just want to look at what you say about
the completion of milestone B.  You say:
"This also meant that [China State]
achieved what the parties contemplated and
anticipated in respect of Milestone B under SA2 and
the TOC for Milestone B should have been issued by
31 December 2019 when works were substantially
completed ..."
Do you see that?
A    Yes.
Q    So in this paragraph, you're asserting
that the works were substantially completed on
31 December 2019, aren't you?
A    For milestone B?
Q    Yes.
A    Yes.
Q    Could we please then go to {D990}.  And if
we could just go, please, to the next page for
a moment, just to see -- this, I think, is a letter
that was written and signed by you, isn't it,
Mr Feng?
A    Yes, correct.
Q    Then please could we go to the first page
again.  You can see that this is dated 17 June 2020,
isn't it?
A    Yes.
Q    Can we just read this letter together
Mr Feng, please.  It says:
"Dear Sir,
"Further to the above mentioned
subject and according to the held meeting by DSOA,
Engineer and CSCEC dated ... 4th June 2020, and
subsequent communication.  Please be informed that
upon the proposed TOC dates which is accepted by
client and engineer.  We would inform our
subcontractors as a record for the agreed TOC dates
in order to follow up contractual matters."
Do you see that?
A    Yes, I saw that.
Q    So the dates that are set out in the box
are dates for TOC that I think were proposed by
China State; is that correct?
A    No, this is not the dates proposed by
China State.  The letter didn't say that the dates
are proposed by China State.  No.
I recall this meeting.  I recall
this, like that's the -- this is the meeting, you
know.
Let me give you a broader background
of this TOC issue, sir.
Q    Well, let's just look at the letter to
begin with, please, Mr Feng, if you don't mind.
A    Sir, let me explain.
Q    No, Mr Feng, you can explain in a moment.
I'd just like to look at the second sentence with
you, please, in light of what you've just said.
A    Please let me explain, then the tribunal
will easily understand what is the --
PRESIDENT:  Mr Feng, let's see if we can
do it this way: Mr Rigney can ask his question,
you answer it, and then give the tribunal
a more general picture.
WITNESS:  Sure, sure, sure.
MR RIGNEY:  Mr Feng, you'll be given
a chance to say what you want to say, I'm sure.
But if you could just help me with this.
I just want your help on a particular point.
A    Okay.
Q    So I'd be very grateful if you could look
at the second sentence of the letter:
"Please be informed that upon
the proposed TOC dates which is accepted by client
and engineer."
Do you see that?
